title: Accelerate cuts into the climax
statement: Build a montage with shot lengths halving 1 s, 0.5 s, 0.25 s, 0.125 s into a mosaic or reveal, then a ~1 s near-silence dip.
evidence: One tier-A round-3 launch film (2.0x, 3% likes, 1.9% bookmarks, 60 real cuts, sync 83%) accelerates exactly so; a tier-C teaser accelerates to 0.125 s under a riser into a calm card at 3.5 s.

evidence: House default informed by practitioner ranges ([H] over [P] in the edit research); no measured beat-edit corpus.

statement: A film may run on 0-4 hard cuts if something changes on screen at least every 3.5 s; score it by motion events, not by ASL.

evidence: One founder-launch guide (practitioner, metrics unsourced) describes no music and no cuts over the opening and calls over-cutting 'nervous'; two cited founder films held 12 s without music and about 30 s with almost no cuts.

evidence: House defaults reconciling practitioner 'every 2-4 s' and 'every 3-5 s' claims and the warning that constant interrupts become the pattern.

title: Scale content to the labelled length
statement: A length setting scales the content: a labelled cut lands within its length and fills it; a '15 s' cut at 80-84 BPM ran 19.6 s, and a 60 s title sequence ran out of names at 34 s and held.

title: Score against a length-matched beat sheet

evidence: Five footage demos of 20-31 s scored against 45-1800 s patterns: a vlog CTA scored 0.4, a founder ask sat at 71% vs 88%+; the length misfit barely moved the score.
